statements.action_statement: No patched mlflow-pipelines release exists on conda-forge. Users should either restrict the tracking server to localhost or a trusted VPN segment, or migrate to the mainline mlflow conda-forge package at >= 2.5.0. Directory traversal payloads can reach this endpoint without authentication, so network-level controls are the only mitigation available at this version.
statements.status_notes: Both CVE-2023-6015 and CVE-2023-3765 affect the same server component at overlapping version ranges. A single upgrade to >= 2.8.1 (the higher of the two fix versions) would remediate both. The conda-forge mlflow-pipelines feedstock should be flagged for EOL or migration guidance.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to mlflow >= 2.5.0 on conda-forge. All conda-forge builds of mlflow prior to 2.5.0 are vulnerable to absolute path traversal allowing unauthenticated read/write of arbitrary server files. Users on older conda-forge builds should update immediately.
statements.status_notes: Fixed in 2.5.0 via commit 6dde937. The vulnerability was disclosed in July 2023. Conda-forge packages at or above 2.5.0 are patched. All historical conda-forge builds below 2.5.0 remain vulnerable.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to mlflow >= 2.8.1 on conda-forge. Historical conda-forge builds of mlflow < 2.8.1 remain vulnerable to unauthenticated arbitrary file write via the MLflow tracking server. Users running older conda-forge builds should update immediately.
statements.status_notes: The fix was introduced in PyPI 2.8.1 via PR #10330 and commit cf83dad. Conda-forge builds at or above 2.8.1 are patched. The current latest conda-forge version (3.12.0) is well past the fix point.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow to version 2.9.2 or later (the current conda-forge latest is 3.12.0, which is not affected). Any conda-forge build prior to 2.9.2 remains vulnerable to this arbitrary file write and potential remote code execution.
statements.status_notes: The database_specific field mentions last_known_affected <= 2.8.1, but the official fix is listed as 2.9.2, meaning 2.9.0 and 2.9.1 may also be affected. The affected_versions list in the advisory includes 2.9.0 and 2.9.1, which is consistent with the fix being in 2.9.2.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow to version 2.9.2 or later (latest conda-forge version is 3.12.0, which is not affected). Older conda-forge builds below 2.9.2 remain vulnerable to this path traversal attack.
statements.status_notes: The fix was released as 2.9.2. The current conda-forge latest (3.12.0) is safe. Historical conda-forge builds below 2.9.2 are genuinely vulnerable.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow to version 2.9.0 or later (the current conda-forge latest is 3.12.0, which is not affected). Conda-forge builds in the 2.x series below 2.9.0 are genuinely vulnerable. Very old 1.x builds may not contain the affected mlflow.data module but should still be upgraded.
statements.status_notes: The mlflow.data module was introduced in MLflow 2.1.0 or thereabouts. The OSV affected range includes all 1.x versions because no explicit 'introduced' version for the vulnerable code was specified, but in practice those builds do not contain mlflow/data/http_dataset_source.py. Maintainers should consider verifying which conda-forge 2.x builds ship this module and refining the affected_versions accordingly.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade the nltk conda-forge package to version 3.9.3 or later (3.9.4 is the latest available on conda-forge) to obtain the fix for the Zip Slip vulnerability in the downloader component.
statements.status_notes: This is a duplicate advisory entry for GHSA-7p94-766c-hgjp (same as the first entry above). Assessment is identical.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to mlflow >= 3.8.1 on conda-forge. All conda-forge builds of mlflow prior to 3.8.1 are potentially vulnerable to command injection via a malicious model artifact when using env_manager=LOCAL for model serving. Users should update to the latest available conda-forge build (currently 3.12.0) which is patched.
statements.status_notes: The advisory details note the vulnerability specifically affects 3.8.0 and is fixed in 3.8.1, but the OSV range covers all versions from 0 to < 3.8.1, meaning older versions are also affected if they contain the same code pattern. The conda-forge latest version 3.12.0 is patched. The fix commits are 361b6f6 and a22ce71.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow-ui to version 3.8.1 or later (e.g., the current conda-forge latest 3.12.0) to obtain the fix. Historical conda-forge builds at versions 2.10.2 through 3.8.0 remain vulnerable to this command injection.
statements.status_notes: The advisory details text states 'The vulnerability affects versions 3.8.0 and is fixed in version 3.8.1', but the OSV range covers all versions from 0 to <3.8.1, indicating the vulnerable code existed across a much wider range. The conda-forge latest version 3.12.0 is patched. Operators running any conda-forge mlflow-ui build older than 3.8.1 should upgrade immediately.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to vllm >= 0.8.5 (conda-forge latest is 0.19.1, which is fixed). If you cannot upgrade, disable or avoid using the Mooncake KV transfer integration entirely, as instances not using Mooncake are not vulnerable.

Users running conda-forge deepdiff versions 5.0.0 through 8.6.0 who pass untrusted user-controlled input to the Delta class should upgrade to deepdiff 8.6.1 or later (conda-forge currently ships 9.1.0, which is safe). The vulnerability requires that attacker-controlled data reaches the Delta constructor; applications not exposing Delta to untrusted input have substantially reduced risk.
statements.status_notes: The fix was committed at https://github.com/seperman/deepdiff/commit/c69c06c13f75e849c770ade3f556cd16209fd183 and released in 8.6.1. conda-forge already ships 9.1.0, so the latest conda-forge build is not vulnerable. The vulnerability is only exploitable when applications pass untrusted input to the Delta class constructor, which is a specific use-case pattern rather than a universal risk. Maintainers of downstream conda packages that use deepdiff's Delta with user input should be notified to upgrade.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade the nltk conda-forge package to version 3.9.3 or later (3.9.4 is the latest available on conda-forge) to address the StanfordSegmenter arbitrary code execution vulnerability. If upgrading immediately is not possible, avoid using the StanfordSegmenter module and do not load JAR files from untrusted or network-accessible paths.
statements.status_notes: This advisory (PYSEC-2026-99 / CVE-2026-0848) is a distinct vulnerability from GHSA-7p94-766c-hgjp despite sharing the same affected version range. The StanfordSegmenter issue has no summary in the OSV record and limited references (only a huntr bounty link), so details are drawn solely from the advisory text. Maintainers should verify whether 3.9.3 actually addresses this specific issue or if a separate patch was applied, as the changelog reference in the other advisory may cover both.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade fastmcp to version 3.2.0 or later (the current conda-forge version 3.3.1 is fixed). All historical conda-forge builds prior to 3.2.0 remain vulnerable to the path traversal / SSRF attack via the OpenAPIProvider's _build_url() method. If upgrading is not immediately possible, avoid using the OpenAPIProvider with untrusted path parameter input.
statements.status_notes: The fix was introduced in v3.2.0 via PR #3507 (commit 40bdfb6b1de0ce30609ee9ba5bb95ecd04a9fb71), which adds `urllib.parse.quote(str(param_value), safe='')` before URL template substitution. The current conda-forge build (3.3.1) is patched. Maintainers should ensure no older pinned conda-forge versions are in active use in production MCP deployments.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade pyspark to 3.3.2 or later (conda-forge latest is 4.1.2). Additionally, ensure that spark.submit.proxyUser.allowCustomClasspathInClusterMode is set to its default of 'false' and cannot be overridden by submitted applications. Environments not using spark-submit with proxy-user (e.g., Apache Livy-managed cluster submissions) are not exposed to this specific attack vector.
statements.status_notes: The PyPI OSV range says 'fixed: 3.3.2' but the advisory text and Maven range both say 3.3.3/3.4.0 are the fix versions. This slight inconsistency means pyspark 3.3.2 may or may not be fully patched — the Maven ecosystem range lists 3.3.2 as still affected. Maintainers should verify whether the PyPI 3.3.2 release contains the security backport. Conda-forge versions 3.4.0 and above are unambiguously safe.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to codechecker >= 6.24.2 once it becomes available on conda-forge. Until then, restrict network access to the CodeChecker server or enforce external authentication controls (e.g., a reverse proxy with auth) to mitigate the authentication bypass risk. Monitor server logs for requests from Anonymous users to endpoints ending in 'Authentication', 'Configuration', or 'ServerInfo' as indicators of exploitation.
statements.status_notes: The fix commit is ad41702e3108e4b92ae5d0143a5b961cc34195eb. Conda-forge should be updated to package codechecker 6.24.2 or later as soon as possible given the critical severity. The `affects_future: true` flag is appropriate since the current conda-forge latest (6.20.0) is still vulnerable and no fixed version is yet available on conda-forge.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow-pipelines to a version based on mlflow >= 2.9.2 when available in conda-forge, or migrate to the standalone mlflow package at >= 2.9.2. Currently no fixed version of mlflow-pipelines exists in the conda-forge channel; version 1.30.0 remains vulnerable to this SSRF attack.
statements.status_notes: This SSRF vulnerability was disclosed later (December 2023) and has a higher fixed-version threshold (2.9.2) than the path traversal CVE. The mlflow-pipelines package appears entirely stagnant at 1.30.0 on conda-forge, leaving users exposed to both this and the path traversal vulnerability with no in-channel remediation path. Users should strongly consider migrating to the standalone mlflow package which receives updates.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade to crawl4ai 0.8.0 or later once available on conda-forge. Until then, users operating the Docker API should disable it, restrict network access, or add authentication to prevent unauthenticated access to the /execute_js, /screenshot, /pdf, and /html endpoints. The vulnerable URL-handling code is present in all conda-forge releases through 0.7.2.
statements.status_notes: The advisory does not explicitly list a fixed version in the OSV ranges, but references v0.8.0 release notes. It is assumed v0.8.0 also addresses this LFI, consistent with the companion advisory. Conda-forge should prioritize packaging v0.8.0. The attack is particularly dangerous in containerized deployments because file:// access to /proc/self/environ can expose secrets injected as environment variables.
